e: Ankylosing spondylitis: young male, inflammatory back pain, morning stiffness, ↓ chest expansion, uveitis (HLA-B27).

Teriparatide (anabolic) is not given before bisphosphonates; it is for severe osteoporosis and an antiresorptive follows it to retain gains.
Ca 1200 mg/day + Vit D₃ is standard.

Posterior hip dislocation (commonest): limb shortened, flexed, adducted, internally rotated; sciatic nerve at risk.
Anterior = abduction + external rotation.
AS: chronic inflammatory back pain, early morning stiffness in <40 y; bilateral heel pain = enthesitis.
Bilateral sacroiliitis + syndesmophytes (marginal bony bridges) → bamboo spine = ankylosing spondylitis.

Anterior = abduction + external rotation.
AS: chronic inflammatory back pain, early morning stiffness in <40 y; bilateral heel pain = enthesitis.
Rickets (Vit D deficiency): bowed legs c̅ widened, frayed, cupped metaphyses.
Radial nerve palsy → wrist drop; cock-up (dynamic) wrist splint c̅ finger-extension outriggers is used.

Bipartite patella: smooth, well-corticated superolateral fragment, often bilateral → X-ray other knee; no fixation.
Fracture has sharp, non-corticated edges.

Carpal tunnel syndrome (median nerve): nocturnal lateral 3½-digit tingling relieved by hanging arm; Durkan's (carpal compression) test.
Froment's = ulnar nerve.
Fibrous dysplasia: ground-glass expansile bone, shepherd's crook deformity + café-au-lait spots (McCune–Albright).

GCT: eccentric epiphyseal–metaphyseal lesion in 20–40 y, commonly around the knee.
Chondroblastoma occurs in open physis (<20 y).
Spondylolisthesis: forward slip of one vertebra over the one below → malalignment of vertebral margins on lateral view.

Pseudogout (CPPD): rhomboid, weakly positively birefringent crystals.
Gout = needle-shaped, negatively birefringent MSU.
Early axial spondyloarthritis (X-ray normal) → MRI SI joints (bone marrow oedema) detects earliest sacroiliitis.
Paget's disease: ↑ hat size, warm bones, bone pain; ALP markedly ↑ c̅ normal Ca, PO₄, PTH.
Compartment syndrome (pain out of proportion, pain on passive stretch, ↓ sensation) → immediate fasciotomy; pulses may be present.
Perthes disease: painless limp in a child due to idiopathic AVN of femoral head; X-ray: sclerosis, flattening, fragmentation.
Fat embolism syndrome (long-bone fracture, 24–72 h): hypoxia, petechiae over chest/conjunctiva, confusion.
